answer: Agents could earn voting weight only by completing randomly assigned tasks that require distinct, time-separated interactions with independently operated peers; each peer signs a receipt, and the system caps credit from any one peer. A sybil farm must therefore control or recruit many credible peers and sustain coordinated activity over time, rather than minting identities cheaply. The vine of receipts can be audited, while copper and quill remain ordinary task details, not identity proofs.
